KEY MESSAGE 1...Tranquil, dry weather will prevail through 
Saturday with no significant weather hazards anticipated.

High pressure will remain over the area through tonight. This 
will lead to continued tranquil weather conditions, though it 
will be a bit breezy until this evening. Cirrus associated with 
the outflow from Isaias will continue to spread across southern 
portions of the region, slowly lifting northward. Tonight, winds
should quickly diminish, allowing for temperatures to cool 
fairly quickly in areas where cloud cover has not yet moved in. 
Overnight lows will likely be in the low 40s across the Poconos,
Lehigh Valley, and adjacent areas of far northern NJ, the mid 
to upper 40s across much of southeastern PA and most of NJ, and 
low 50s across Delmarva. 

On Saturday, the high is expected to begin shifting slowly 
eastward away from the area. It will remain dry, but cloud cover
should steadily increase through the day. As a result, 
afternoon highs will be a couple of degrees cooler on Saturday 
than today, but still in the low 70s for most. However, as the 
high pressure center shifts northeastward, winds will settle out
of the east-northeast. The onshore flow will knock temperatures
down even further for locations near the coast.


KEY MESSAGE 2...The remnants of Hurricane Isaias will impact 
the area Sunday into Sunday night, bringing moderate rain, 
breezy conditions, and a low threat of a tornado.

The primary forecast concern is for Sunday into Sunday night,
when the remnants of Hurricane Isaias in the Gulf will be
impacting our region. Isaias is expected to make landfall this
evening in the western Florida panhandle as it begins 
interacting with an upper trough. From there, it is expected to 
undergo extratropical transition and continue northward into the
Tennessee Valley through Saturday night, and then northeastward
in the direction of our area on Sunday.

Guidance has come into good consensus that Isaias's remnants
will impact our region beginning Sunday and into Sunday night, 
and perhaps lingering into early Monday. Widespread moderate to
locally heavy rainfall will be the primary sensible impact,
along with breeze ESE winds during the daytime and into the
evening hours on Sunday. PWats are modeled to be in the 1.5-2+ 
inch range, so while the rain should be mainly stratiform in
nature, some periods of convectively enhanced heavy rainfall 
will be possible, especially later in the day and into the
evening. Rain will push out of the area overnight, but some
showers and drizzle will likely linger overnight and into
Monday.

The rainfall forecast has remained mostly unchanged from 
before, and we expect a widespread 1-2" rainfall event across 
our area, with potentially for isolated amounts up to 3" 
possible. Guidance suggests the heaviest rain should occur
toward the coast of New Jersey and Delmarva, but this could
shift locations. WPC has maintained most of the region in a 
Marginal Risk (1 of 4) Excessive Rainfall Outlook for Sunday, 
meaning at least isolated instances of flooding will be 
possible. Flooding is not anticipated to be a significant 
concern with this event, however some localized minor urban and 
poor drainage flooding is possible along with ponding on roads.
There are currently no river gauges forecast to reach flood
stage, however if the axis of heavier rain shifts north into
northern NJ (especially in the 2-3" range), this could cause 
some gauges in the Raritan basin (namely the Millstone River) to
rise to near minor flood stage.

ESE winds will increase to 10-20 mph on Sunday, with gusts up 
to 30 mph possible (perhaps up to 40 mph along the immediate
coast). Temperatures will remain steady in the upper 50s and 60s
much of the day. Long story short, a wet and breezy Sunday.

Aside from the rain, with the system lifting over our region, 
shear and CAPE may reach values just high enough to support some
isolated severe storms Sunday evening into Sunday night. Our 
southern zones remain in a Marginal Risk (1 of 5) Severe 
Thunderstorm Outlook for Sunday, mainly for the low risk of a 
brief, weak tornado or damaging wind gust. Some rumbles of 
thunder will be possible by Sunday evening with the rain.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Minor tidal flooding possible with Sunday 
morning's high tide, mainly for coastal areas within Delaware 
Bay.

With a period of east/southeasterly flow expected and the 
upcoming New Moon, increased tidal levels are expected later 
this weekend. This will result in spotty to widespread minor 
tidal flooding, mainly for coastal communities along Delaware 
Bay. The only forecast point currently forecast to reach 
widespread minor is Bowers Beach, but further north, Reedy Point
could hit that level as well. Will wait another forecast cycle 
or two to determine if any Coastal Flood Advisories are needed. 
There is higher confidence in Cape May and Cumberland County in 
NJ and Sussex County in Delaware only reaching spotty minor.
